subject: Private BYOK: split custody runthrough and emergency unseal plan
messages:
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, security@finco-payments.com, ops_team@finco-payments.com
Date: 2028-11-09T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Private BYOK: split custody runthrough and emergency unseal plan

Team / FinCo folks —

Per the upcoming cutover window (Nov 20) FinCo has asked for a joint runthrough focused on two areas we haven't fully rehearsed together: 1) split-key custody (4-of-6 quorum with remote keepers) and 2) emergency unseal / zeroize workflow when the operator plane is offline. This is a compliance gating item for their legal team and SOC reviewer.

Please review the attached checklist and topology diagram before our runthrough. Specific asks from FinCo:
- Confirm we can support a split-key ceremony with two out-of-band escrow devices (air-gapped USB) that FinCo controls.
- Demonstrate emergency unseal that does not require Redwood console access (serial or signed JWT via HSM proxy).
- Show network policy (iptables/NACL) that restricts egress to vendor CA endpoints and our KMS proxy IPs only.

Proposed attendees: Vivek (private deployment lead), Jonas (network), Priyom (platform ops), Marissa (security eng), plus FinCo security/ops contacts.

Can we schedule a 90-minute dry run next week? Suggest Tue 2028-11-14 10:00-11:30 PT. If that works I'll send calendar invites and a short script for the ceremony steps.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(kim@redwood.ai)

Attachments: 20281109-kms-runbook-checklist.pdf, topology-diagram-kms-segmentation.png
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, security@finco-payments.com
Date: 2028-11-09T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private BYOK: split custody runthrough and emergency unseal plan

Kim — thanks for the note. Tue 11/14 10:00 PT works for me. A few quick clarifications and constraints from our side: 

1) Hardware HSM: we support both Thales Luna and vendor-managed cloud HSMs behind our KMIP proxy, but for an on-prem BYOK FinCo asked for FIPS 140-2 Level 3 attestations and hardware presence. The plan to include two air-gapped USB escrow devices is fine; however, we recommend using sealed backup tokens (PKCS#11 wrapped) rather than raw keys on USB to avoid accidental exposure.

2) Quorum model: We can configure a 4-of-6 quorum where Redwood holds no more than two key shares. FinCo must nominate at least two remote keepers who control physical escrow devices. We'll script the ceremony so that no single operator can reconstruct the full key.

3) Emergency unseal: There are two approved paths — (A) serial-console-initiated unseal using a signed one-time JWT that the HSM validates against an offline public key; (B) operator-driven unseal via out-of-band escrow retrieval. We should rehearse both. Note: path A assumes the HSM firmware accepts a signed CSR token over the management channel; confirm with Thales on the call.

I'll prepare a short demo harness that executes a split-key restore using our KMIP proxy and shows the audit log entries in the console. Priyom — can you verify that the KMIP proxy currently rejects any client that doesn't present an mTLS cert from our operator CA? We need that check in place for the demo.

— Vivek
VP, Private Deployments
From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, thales-sales@vendor.example
Date: 2028-11-10T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private BYOK: split custody runthrough and emergency unseal plan

Looping in a networking note and vendor questions.

Network posture we should demonstrate:
- No outbound internet from the HSM or KMIP proxy; NAT is allowed only from the management bastion for vendor updates.
- Egress allowed to: vendor attestation CA IP ranges, Redwood telemetry endpoints (TLS, on-prem metric relay), and FinCo CA ocsp endpoints.
- KMS proxy must enforce client SAN matching (operator@redwood) and reject any connection that doesn't present the correct mTLS identity.

Questions for Thales (copied):
- Can the HSM validate a signed JWT over the serial management channel or do we need vendor-signed extension?
- What's the supported mechanism for a sealed-wrapped backup token (PKCS#11 wrapped blob) and the recommended key wrapping algorithm for air-gapped transport?

I've attached a rough topology PNG showing a three-segment design: management bastion (jump host), HSM VLAN with strict ACLs, and workload VLAN for inference nodes. We'll walk that diagram in the runthrough.

-Jonas
Principal Network Engineer
From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, ops_team@finco-payments.com, security@finco-payments.com
Date: 2028-11-11T13:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private BYOK: split custody runthrough and emergency unseal plan

Thanks — prepping ops checklist and a minimal test harness. A few operational items we need on record before the demo: 

- Ticket gating: every key ceremony step must be performed under an open ticket (JIRA SUP-4512) with screenshots and signed approvals. We'll include a time-stamped audit snapshot to prove separation of duties.

- Zeroize test: we will run a simulated zeroize on a non-production HSM replica. That action will demonstrate the audit trail and the automated operator eviction hooks. Note: we will never run zeroize on production hardware without explicit FinCo exec signoff.

- Recovery SLA: propose a 4-hour maximum RTO for full key reconstruction from escrow in the event of catastrophic failure, with a documented checklist for the FinCo keepers.

- Console-less unseal path: I'll stub out the one-time signed JWT generator. For the demo we'll use a test signing key that the HSM recognizes; the production flow will use FinCo-controlled signing keys and our attestation of the token's validity.

Action items before Tue runthrough:
1) Thales to confirm serial/JWT acceptance or provide alternate vendor guidance (thales-sales@vendor.example).
2) FinCo to confirm which two escrow keepers will attend and their process for physical key delivery.
3) Redwood ops to build demo wallet with wrapped backup tokens and mTLS certs in place.

I'll attach a small script (unseal-escrow-instructions.txt) that walks the team through the scripted restore.

— Priyom
Platform Operations
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@finco-payments.com, ops_team@finco-payments.com
Date: 2028-11-12T15:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private BYOK: split custody runthrough and emergency unseal plan

All — quick confirmation following the vendor reply. Thales confirmed in writing that: 
- The HSM supports validation of signed tokens over the management channel using a vendor-provided attestation extension. They provided a firmware minimum version which Priyom will validate against our test unit.
- Their recommended wrapped backup format is PKCS#11 wrapped blob using AES-KW with a vendor CA-wrapped KEK. For air-gapped transfer we should use the wrapped blob + X.509 signature from the FinCo keeper.

Given that, FinCo security: can you confirm the two keepers and that they are comfortable with the PKCS#11 wrapped-blob approach? Also, please confirm you have a private room for the split-key ceremony (camera off) and an IT person to present the physical USB escrow devices to the operator.

Next steps: Kimberly will send the calendar invite for Tue 2028-11-14 10:00 PT and a 6-step script. We'll run the demo on our staging HSM and produce an artifact bundle (audit logs, signed zeroize test report).

Thanks everyone — looking forward to a smooth run.
